svg.text: Teryx OS wiring, sheet 'lights'. Made from config/wiring.yaml by `python -m teryx wiring`. Don't edit this file.
Labels: wire id, size, fuse (if the wire has its own), and anything in between. Faded = optional. Hover for notes. Full table: docs/wiring/README.md

g.title: LT17: FB.F3 -> FLOOD_L.pos - Always live, the MOSFET switches the - side
LT23: FB.IN -> FB2.IN - Own 30 A inline fuse off the 12-way's feed stud
LT28: BTS4.M+ -> HEAD_L.LO - light.head_l_low. The diode stops the backup toggle feeding back into the BTS7960
LT44: PCA.PWM15 -> BTS4.EN - R_EN + L_EN joined, 10k to ground
LT48: BRAKE_SW.OUT -> TAIL_L.STOP - Brake lights always work, whatever the Pico does
LT51: LIMP_SW.OUT -> HEAD_L.LO - Backup toggle on = low beams at full, even with the control box dead
LT54: LIMP_SW.OUT -> TAIL_L.TAIL - Tails on with the backup toggle too
LT62: LIMP_SW.OUT -> TRAILER.P7_TAIL - Trailer tail lights on the backup toggle too
LT63: FB2.F6 -> BRAKE_SW.IN - Brake switch feed, always live
LT58: PCA.PWM13 -> BTS9.RPWM - light.beacon: flashed at 3 Hz by the Pico
LT60: PCA.PWM14 -> BTS9.LPWM - light.beacon_white: 3 Hz, opposite amber, stopped only
LT64: PICO.3V3 -> BTS4.VCC - Logic supply, like BTS1-3

FB: Blade fuse block - 12 fuses in use. Small loads that can go out together share a fuse (front bars in pairs, trailer tail + stop, interior bar + accessory). All four front bars are NOT on one fuse, so one fault can't black out the front at night. The winch, control box power, key, power hold and each actuator keep their own. Sam's 12-way (in the post) is used, so it is full with no spares; add a small 6-way next to it if more circuits come
g.text: F7 extras - interior bar + relay 7 acc…

g.title: FB2: Small 6-way blade fuse block (stock lights + beacon) - Next to the 12-way, which is full. Fed off the 12-way's feed stud through its own 30 A fuse. All 6 ways used (way 6 feeds the stock brake switch so the brake lights are on a known fuse, always live)

g.title: RELAYS: 16-ch relay board, channels 1-8 - One 16-channel board of mechanical 5 V relays with opto and JD-VCC jumper (AliExpress cart), in an aux box next to the control box. RELAYS2 is channels 9-16 of the same board. The solid state G3MB-202P board Sam has is AC only and won't turn off on 12 V DC. JD-VCC jumper off, coils on 5 V, inputs from 3.3 V
FLOOD_L: Rear flood left (4 in pod) - Outside of the roll cage mounting plate. Also the reverse light. Dimmable on MOSFET channel 7 (left) and 8 (right)
FLOOD_R: Rear flood right (4 in pod)

BTS4: BTS7960 4 (left headlight low / high) - Used as two high-side switches, not a motor bridge. VCC from the Pico 3.3 V like BTS1-3. EN (R_EN + L_EN) from PCA9685 PWM15 with a 10k to ground, so the lamps stay off until the Pico is running
BTS9: BTS7960 9 (roof beacon amber / white) - Two-colour beacons usually share one earth wire, so the colours are switched on the + side like the stock lamps: RPWM amber, LPWM white

LIMP_SW: Backup lights toggle (hidden) - The Teryx has no headlight switch, so the dash and the Pico do everything. This hidden toggle is the backup if the control box dies: it feeds both low beams, both tails and the trailer tail at full through diodes. Leave it off normally. The Pico also turns low beams and tails on by itself if the dash goes quiet with the key on
BRAKE_SW: Brake light switch (stock) - Also feeds both brake filaments and the trailer stop pin through diodes, so the brake lights work at full even with the control box off

MOSFET: 8-ch isolated MOSFET board (low side, all 8 used) - Sam's board: 8-channel opto-isolated MOSFET driver, DC 3.7-27 V, 10 A per channel, PWM input 3-20 V, 0-20 kHz. 1-4 front bars, 5 cabin bar, 6 trailer bar, 7-8 rear floods. Low side switching, so each light's + comes from its fuse and its - goes to an OUT pin
HEAD_L: Left headlight (stock, 12 V 35/35 W) - Dual filament bulb, low and high, one shared earth (Kawasaki 2013 Teryx 750 owner's manual: headlight 12 V 35/35 W x 2)

PCA: PCA9685 16-ch PWM board (0x40) - Every light that isn't a front bar or the cabin bar dims through this (docs/lights.md). Wires soldered straight to the pads, no header pins. VCC 3.3 V so the outputs are 3.3 V, which the MOSFET boards (3-20 V input) and the BTS7960s (3.3 V logic like BTS1-3) take. Leave V+ (servo power) empty. OE tied low on the board. PWM0 trailer bar, 1-10 stock lights on BTS7960 4-8, 11-12 rear floods, 13-14 beacon amber / white on BTS7960 9, 15 BTS7960 enable. All outputs are off at power-up
TAIL_L: Left tail / brake light (stock, 12 V 8/27 W) - Dual filament bulb, 8 W tail and 27 W brake, one shared earth (owner's manual: tail/brake light 12 V 8/27 W x 2)
TAIL_R: Right tail / brake light (stock, 12 V 8/27 W)

BEACON: Roof beacon (amber + white LED, steady-on) - Sam's amber + white LED beacon (bought 18 Nov). Each colour stays on steady and the Pico flashes them at 3 Hz (NZ Vehicle Lighting Rule 11.1(2): 2 to 4 Hz), amber and white taking turns. White only when stopped: on the road only red or amber may show to the rear. Fits Sam's existing hole on the roof
TRAILER: 7-pin flat trailer socket (Narva 82043BL, reed switch)
PICO: Raspberry Pi Pico 2 - Talks to the Pi over CAN only. No USB lead to the Pi; reflash with a laptop on its own USB port in the workshop
